targetText: By concentration we understand the increase of capital that is due to the capitalisation of the surplus value produced by that capital; under centralisation we understand the joining together of various individual capital units which thus form a new larger unit.
summary: Concentration grows capital through reinvesting surplus value, while centralization merges existing capitals into giant trusts and state-capitalist blocs.
explanation: Bukharin applies Marx's laws of concentration and centralization to the world economy, showing how national economies coalesce into competing 'state-capitalist trusts' that wage war to centralize territory.
